T741 is mechanically right that edge 5 gates promotion not dispatch; W3-02 still goes early because a Wave-2 promotion taken on a stale matrix must be redone.

6.3 SHARPEST: whether 'no UNTESTED survives' is a finish condition (T742 rule R3) or whether NA:<named blocker> is a completed disposition (T740 W3-07). Incompatible. 21 rows are UNTESTED, several because the instrument does not exist. Recommend T740's; R3 would force either a large unbudgeted measurement programme or a dishonest status change, and DIRECTION asks for re-derived/demoted/retired, not proven. Mitigation: every NA: cell must name what would change it, and W3-18 surfaces the whole NA: set in one place.

new_findings_this_synthesis.summary: C8 — the gate guarding every promotion Waypoint 3 exists to make — is VACUOUS today and reads clean.
new_findings_this_synthesis.detail: src/claimlint.zig counts a C8 violation only for claims at PROVEN (verified at :2982; its own calibration arm 9b asserts the CLAIMED silence deliberately). Every kernel claim is held at CLAIMED by Amendment-2 edge 5. So the run prints 'kernel-function claims in kill matrix: 3 / with at least one unkilled mutant: 3 / at PROVEN (violation): 0' and the SUMMARY line prints 'C8 mutation-adequacy violations 0'. C8 therefore reads 0 because Waypoint 3 has not run, not because the mutants are killed — and it will fire, on a matrix three lanes already know is stale, at the exact moment Waypoint 3 first tries to promote something.
new_findings_this_synthesis.evidence: bin/weizigo-claimlint at HEAD 2ec4f93, C8 section and SUMMARY; src/claimlint.zig:2075-2127,2982; docs/epics/E1-markovian/sprints/verify-battery/pass1/kill-matrix.json (total_mutants 10, mutants_killed 3)

ranking.basis: Structural completeness and executability of the row set, weighted by whether its factual base survives verification. T740 first: chosen as trunk, every number reproduced, only lane whose gate carries its own seeded controls. T743 second: deepest coverage, exact census, and the two best row-quality contributions (row-ID enumeration, live-hold check) — but its largest row is obviated by a ruling it did not read. T742 third: fewest rows and one wrong hold, but the single most valuable correction in the race, and its gate-first instinct was right. T744 fourth: the only unique substantive find and the best definitions, but 2 of 13 rows obviated and the thinnest gate. T741 fifth on the row set alone — highest density and best Amendment-2 analysis, but it is the one lane whose row set is unsafe to execute as written (no kill-matrix row, no artifact row), and both gaps trace to trusting a green reading.
ranking.caveat: One row each; n=1 per model. This ranks five documents, not five models. The ordering of T742/T744/T741 is close and the tie-breaks are judgement calls, and T741's fifth place is a statement about two specific gaps, not about density or reasoning quality, on which it scored highest.

race_i_comparison.convergence_as_a_signal: Five independent lanes agreed on: the ladder is evidentiary/shake-out order and never a dispatch gate (all 5); the phantom --bundle row must close and the audit must NOT be re-executed (all 5); the mutation kill matrix is contradictory and must be reconciled (4 of 5 — T741 dissenting, and wrongly); the finish line must be an exit code and not prose (all 5); file ownership and not the wave number is the real serializer (all 5); no worker holds CLAIMS.md (4 of 5). That convergence is itself evidence the brief's four sections were unambiguous, and it is why the disagreements in §6 are worth the operator's attention: they are the places five independent readings did NOT converge.
